title: Lorena V. Roelke - The Post-Crescent
content: Lorena “Rena” Valeria Roelke (nee Meisel), age 94, passed away on October 16, 2026, at Ballard Glenn in Appleton. She was born July 31, 1932, to Edmund and Dorothy (Ubbelohde) Meisel. Rena married Frank Roelke, Jr. with whom she shared 59 years until his passing in 2013. Rena is survived by children: Russ (Lynn), Cyndi (Jim) Thaldorf, and Judy (David) Sprink. Grandmother of Tom (Adrianne) Schmidt, Anne Roelke; Kelli (Dain) Peer, Eric (Shaye) Thaldorf; Hannah Sprink and Paige Sprink; and 8 great grandchildren, plus one on the way. Paul (Lucy) Meisel; sister Audrey (Jess) Bundensen, brother-in-law Wayne Hiller, as well as Franks siblings and parents. title: Ligue 1: PSG v Lyon at Parc des Princes moved to Monday as Paris prepares for another weekend of protests - BBC
content: Paris St-Germain fans celebrated winning the Champions League near the Eiffel Tower in May 2026 Paris St-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been pushed back 24 hours to Monday as the French capital prepares for another weekend of protests. The fixture at the Parc des Princes in Paris had been scheduled to kick off at 19:45 GMT on Sunday but will instead take place at 20:30 on Monday. The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) announced the postponement in a statement, external on Friday after French police prohibited the fixture from taking place on its original date. French authorities are preparing a major security operation for demonstrations planned for Saturday. Around 550,000 people took part in demonstrations last Saturday to protest rising fuel prices, education standards and the cost of living, which have escalated after weeks of student protests. Marches took place in several major French cities, including Paris, backed by unions and student groups, and were marred by some incidents of violence, looting and destruction. The security challenge is further complicated by Sunday's NFL match between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, an event expected to require a significant police deployment. The game will be played in Saint-Denis, about 10km from Place de la Bastille, where the protests are expected to begin. The disruptions have already affected France's domestic football schedule with Toulouse's Ligue 1 home game against Troyes moved from Saturday to Sunday at the request of authorities. Reigning French and European champions PSG are second in the standings after seven matches, while Lyon lead the table on 14 points, ahead of the holders on goal difference. The match will also now be played on the same day as the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. Injured PSG pair Ousmane Dembele, the 2025 winner, and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are among the contenders for the award. PSG on different level - but where do they rank against other great sides? title: Tottenham Hotspur Women v Arsenal Preview - Arseblog News
content:
Arteta: ‘Unique’ Dowman will get chances ‘in the right moments’ Arteta hails squad chemistry as competition for places grows ‘It can and must be better’ Slegers seeking improvement in North London Derby Guimaraes hails “unbelievable” Rice as midfield understanding grows THE LOWDOWN
Arsenal travel to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to play Spurs in the WSL on Saturday lunchtime. The Gunners have endured a horrendous start to the season and sit in 8th place in the WSL table. Last weekend’s draw at home to Birmingham City compounded a start to the season that has made the WSL title impossible and Champions League qualification now feels like a tall order too. Spurs have lost their last two games against London City Lionesses and Chelsea and conceded six goals in each game. In my experience, when that happens to a team they tend to overcorrect and focus on defensive stability- this is exactly what we saw in September when Manchester United ground out a 1-1 draw at Emirates Stadium on the back of a thrashing at the hands of Chelsea. In one respect, Spurs shouldn’t present the sort of low block that has been Arsenal’s kryptonite this season. On the other, it probably wouldn’t be a huge surprise if Spurs made the calculation that two very leaky defensive performances allied to Arsenal’s issue with low defensive blocks might inspire a change of approach. It feels a bit trite to say that Arsenal have to win, Arsenal always have to win. But in the midst of this current crisis, it feels like they have been in ‘if they don’t win this the manager might get sacked’ territory for several weeks now. Renee Slegers’ side have won two games this season, both 1-0. There simply has to be a drastic uptick in results and performances and that has to happen now, now, now and now. Chloe Kelly (hamstring) is still out. Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang are all absent with knee injuries. Kim Little is still out with a small muscle injury, while Frida Maanum (quad) is still out, as is Mariona (hamstring) and Selina Cerci (knee). Daphne van Domselaar will return to the match day squad following a knee injury but will not start the game. Available squad
Goalkeepers: 1.van Domselaar 16.Misa 28.Borbe 40.Damm
Defenders: 2.Fox 3.Wubben-Moy 5.De Almeida 6.Williamson(c) 7.Catley 22.O.Batlle 24.Hinds 31.Holmberg
Midfielders: 4.Stanway 14.Reuteler 32.Cooney-Cross
Forwards: 9.Foord 11.Smith 19.Baum 23.Russo 25.Blackstenius Unavailable: 8.Mariona 10.Little 12.L.Maanum 17.Agyemang 18.Kelly 26.Reid 29.Cerci A WORD FROM THE BOSS
‘Spurs play high risk high reward football and that’s their identity. I can’t go into the coaches minds and into their camp and what they’re thinking. I would say they have a strong identity and will want to play the way they have been playing. Against us, it could be possible that they want to stop things. Let’s see tomorrow we’ll have to be prepared for both. ‘We have sold out the away section. So that’s that’s where our focus is. We need to fight tomorrow on that pitch for 90+ minutes and we need to do it for the fans because we know that it’s been tough times for them as well. We wanted much more for them and seeing that we sell out the away section for this game after the run of games we’ve had, that’s going to be our biggest fuel in the game to be there and give absolutely everything on the pitch for the fans tomorrow. ‘It’s been a good week and we’ve finally had some time and it’s not only about talking and meeting and those things for us. It’s been more about actions. And so we’ve had a really good training week where we’ve rescheduled a little bit and we’ve really had the time spend on the pitch. So that’s been really good for us and today we had a very sharp session and we look forward to tomorrow.’ LAST TIME OUT
When the teams met in the away match last season, Spurs held Arsenal to a 0-0 draw at Brisbane Road. At Emirates Stadium in March the Gunners ran out 5-2 winners thanks to a Russo hat-trick and goals from Foord and Blackstenius. Spurs started the season in very strong shape, winning 10 points from their first four games. However, the last two matches have brought some chastening lessons with a 6-1 defeat to London City Lionesses and a 6-2 defeat to Chelsea. Under current manager Martin Ho, Spurs have firmly moved into the category of a team that expects to challenge for Champions League qualification. Spurs have upped their game in the investment stakes when it comes to their women’s team. Former Manchester United assistant coach Martin Ho’s appointment to the Head Coach position in the summer of 2025 also yielded a clear strategy that saw Tottenham increase their spending on recruitment. Big players like Alice Sombath, Amanda Nilden, Signe Gaupset, Cathinka Tandberg, Olivia Holdt, Shekeira Martinez, Julie Blakstad, Kirsty Hanson and Victoria Pelova have joined to bolster the squad. Spurs now have a host of elite international talent to call upon. However, in recent games, a midfield of Gaupset and Pelova has been too easy for opponents to run through. In Martinez and Kirsty Hanson Spurs have brought in two of the best counter attacking attackers in the WSL and given Arsenal’s issues defending transitions recently, this will be an area to watch. Alessia Russo scored a hat trick the last time Arsenal and Spurs met in March and the case for playing her in a deeper role seems to be fading by the week. She had scored away at Paris FC and Manchester City prior to the international break this month, before scoring in both games for England against Greece during the international period. Russo was played in the number 10 position in the 1-1 draw with Birmingham, a decision Slegers admitted that she deliberated over, ‘with Less, she is such a good 9 and she’s done so well for England, so it was a really tough decision to say, what do we do with Less now? What’s best for the team? And we had a good conversation with Less, so she played in the 10.’ Quite simply, there can be no more of this in the short term. Russo is a 9 and is in scoring form. Even with Maanum injured, Gery Reuteler was brought into the club this summer, there is plenty of cover in the position behind the striker. Russo can absolutely play as a 10 but sooner or later you have to build around her as a 9. There are plenty of other number 10s in the squad. Wasn’t the word around the last game that Kim had been ill?   how she “still injured” Well now we know the actuality – and Kim is a big loss but Olivia seems right back on form & it’s time for Alessia to show up with a goal or 3! Russo needs to be 9 over SB so Reuteler be the 10 or swap with Stanway. I….the derby could be the master stroke. If we don’t win (loss or draw) then it only serves to lengthen the uncertainty and probably we’ll see a ‘push come to shove’ moment. If we win it could be the catapult to rescue whats left of the season. We still got 2 trophies to fight for. ..the league might be gone but if we derail ourselves then we can expect to chuck out of both cups and chuck out embarrassingly. But hope springs eternal and I’ll be on a train first thing tomorrow morning. title: Fashion Is the Future of Technology: How V of BTS, Navy Blue, Kelela and Nothing Are Bridging Tech and Culture — ‘Find Joy in the Little Things’ - Yahoo
content: Technology and fashion have always been intertwined, but as more of the devices we use become things we wear, the line between the two is getting harder to distinguish. Headphones are an obvious example. Once primarily functional accessories, they've become part of how people present themselves in public. Whether worn over the ears, resting around the neck, or sitting on a purse or a hat, they can complement an outfit, communicate personal taste and signal an affinity for a particular brand or community. Like sneakers, jewelry, socks or a favorite bag, they're increasingly part of the visual language through which people express themselves and story tell. John Legend to Appear With Democratic Ohio Gov. Candidate Amy Acton Amid Backlash Against Opponent's 'Deeply Troubling' Ad Best Last-Minute Halloween Costume Ideas Inspired by 2026's Biggest Music & Pop Culture Moments Charli xcx Books Cameo in Martin Scorsese Thriller Starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence And it makes sense. When technology becomes something you physically wear, its design becomes part of your appearance. You're not just choosing a device for what it can do. You're choosing something that will exist on your body, in public, alongside everything else you use to communicate who you are and what you're about. And now you're thinking, "Will these headphones match most of my looks? Will these headphones bring my fits together or take away from them?" We're at a point where so many headphones have amazing noise-canceling, transparency mode, great audio quality and mics. Some may be better than others in some categories but the differences — no matter if the brands like it or not — are becoming few and far between. That raises a bigger question about the future of technology: As products become increasingly capable, will their cultural significance matter as much as their technical capabilities? At Nothing's New Noise event in New York, that question extended beyond the products on display. The event brought together technology, fashion and music, with conversations featuring Kelela and Navy Blue — two artists whose approaches to music and fashion offer different perspectives on where culture is heading. The connection isn't simply that musicians are wearing headphones or that technology companies are borrowing from fashion. It's that technology, fashion and music are increasingly intertwined forms of self-expression. The products we carry, the clothes we wear and the music we listen to all contribute to how we construct our identities and how people construct identities for us. And as technology becomes more visible in our everyday lives, the way it looks, feels and fits into our personal worlds becomes harder to separate from its function. For Nothing's chief brand officer, Charlie Smith, that relationship is already apparent in the way people wear headphones. "Headphones are like wearing a scarf or a necklace," he says. "I think it says something about who you are as a person, in the same way that the brands of clothes you choose to wear do." Smith, who previously worked at fashion house Loewe, sees an opportunity for technology to develop the same kind of recognizable identity that fashion brands have cultivated for decades. He argues that many devices have become visually interchangeable, creating space for companies to distinguish themselves through more expressive design. Philipp Von Lintel, who works on Nothing's product design, makes the comparison even more directly: "The Headphone 1 is almost like a sneaker, but for your head." It's a simple analogy with larger implications. Sneakers aren't just designed around comfort and performance. Their silhouettes, materials and cultural associations can make them objects of desire, personal expression and community, as someone who collects with close to 250+ pairs, trust me I know. Headphones can occupy similar territory because they're functional objects that people also wear as part of their everyday look. But fashion's influence on technology isn't just about making devices look better. It's also about the experience of interacting with them, the materials, the craftsmanship and the consideration behind their design. Navy Blue, who describes himself as detail-oriented, says those considerations are what make products meaningful to him. "I think there are a lot of like-minded people who find joy in the little things, like how their T-shirt might have a single stitch, and so forth," he says. He believes consumers will increasingly want to understand how products are made, including where their materials come from. In that sense, technology's relationship with fashion could involve more than aesthetics. It could also mean bringing the values associated with craftsmanship and intentional design into the products people use every day. And this is where the conversation about technology starts to intersect with the future of music. The connection between fashion, technology and music is also reflected in the people brands choose to represent them. At Nothing's New Noise event, the company announced V of BTS as its new global brand ambassador alongside the launch of Headphone (1) Pro. The partnership illustrates how technology companies are increasingly looking to music and culture to give their products an identity beyond their technical capabilities. V isn't simply representing a pair of headphones; he's bringing his own creative identity and global cultural influence into the way the product is presented to audiences. Artists have long used their visual identities to complement their sound, turning clothing, photography, performance and album artwork into extensions of their creative worlds. But as Kelela points out, that relationship only works when the visual expression has something meaningful behind it. "Sometimes it's really great because the world-building you do around a certain type of sound helps guide you toward understanding what somebody means," she says. "It helps you receive the sonic outcome even more." She also cautions that a strong visual identity can become an empty shell if there's nothing substantive behind it musically. That tension matters to both industries. Fashion can give technology a stronger identity, just as visual presentation can deepen the experience of music. But neither can rely on appearances alone. The design must mean something, and the music has to deliver something worth hearing. For artists like Kelela and Navy Blue, that connection between appearance, identity and creative substance is part of a broader conversation about where culture is going. Their perspectives at New Noise offered a reminder that the future isn't just about the next device or the next sound. It's also about the people creating new ways for audiences to experience both. title: Grand Theft Auto V – The Legacy Review - IGN
content: I’m taking a look back at each of the core Grand Theft Auto games and replaying them in the lead-up to the arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6. What we’ll be putting together won’t be traditional re-reviews, and they won’t come with any new IGN score, but they will re-examine what made each GTA remarkable upon the time of its release. By the end of the project, using GTA’s previously six-star wanted level, you should be able to get an idea of where each of these games roughly rank in my long-term love for this series. Our last stop in this series is Grand Theft Auto V: a game so nice, they released it thrice. 13 years. Three console generations. 230 million copies. Over $10 billion in revenue. The numbers that tell the story of Grand Theft Auto V’s longevity and success are wildly impressive and virtually unprecedented. The only other games even in the conversation are Minecraft or, depending on your criteria, about 200 different versions of Tetris. The numbers, however, don’t tell us why GTA V still sells more copies every few months than most games will ever total. They don’t tell us why people can’t get enough of it, and they don’t tell us why it’s special. So how did we get here? I guess it was the weather. While GTA IV’s Liberty City sandbox was a dense, modestly-sized, and entirely urban environment, GTA V’s vision of the city of Los Santos was considerably more sprawling and varied. Yes, it retained a grid-like downtown district packed with tall buildings and a few particularly sizable skyscrapers, but Los Santos otherwise has a wholly different identity to that of Liberty City – and the map encompasses an area way beyond Los Santos itself. The aesthetic shift is stark. Weather depending, the beating San Andreas sunshine gives vehicles a dazzling gleam, casts crisp shadows, and saturates the whole place with a sharp, sun-bleached vibe. It’s not the stylised orange tint that illustrated the oppressive heat of 1992 Los Santos in GTA: San Andreas, but it’s bright, effective, and a striking visual departure from the cold, drab, and gritty appearance of Liberty City. It’s also such a different place to explore. The town is splintered into dozens of distinct districts that seamlessly blend from one to the next – from the affluent mansions of Vinewood Hills and Richman to the spectacle of Vinewood itself, glowing under a thin layer of grime and entertainment industry sleaze, and from the sun-kissed sand and beach bum backalleys of ageing Vespucci to the graffiti-tagged and struggling suburbs of South Los Santos. Outside Los Santos, the countryside opens up to include desert, forest, mountains, and a handful of other small towns dotted around the map. It’s essentially a greatly expanded vision of the southern segment of GTA: San Andreas’ map – the section that features Los Santos, Mount Chiliad, and its immediate surroundings. It’s actually more than twice the size of GTA: San Andreas in its entirety, even if it doesn’t always feel that way, considering you can’t travel beyond the fringe of the county to find a fully-fledged San Fierro or Las Venturas. However, that’s more of a statement about how utterly special GTA: San Andreas’ map really is, rather than an indictment of GTA V in any real way. That is, GTA V’s map remains a stunning achievement. It’s a world that – even after 13 years – I’m still spotting signs, storefronts, and subtleties that I don’t think I’ve overtly noticed before. Like all the best developers, Rockstar understands that true immersion emerges through accumulation: a single graffiti-tagged wall, bill-covered pole, or interesting piece of architecture might not be hugely remarkable on its own, but combined they become something else altogether. Funnily enough, a world full of thousands of such details can make an entire city so realistic you essentially stop noticing it. It’s almost counterintuitive; things don’t stand out, because they look so authentic, lived-in, and normal. The smartest way Rockstar exploits this densely detailed map is through GTA V’s defining innovation: its trio of protagonists. You swap between Michael De Santa, a retired criminal becoming increasingly agitated at his otherwise comfortable suburban life; Franklin Clinton, an aspiring, small-time hustler looking for a real payday to get him out of his rundown neighbourhood; and Trevor Philips, a wildly volatile Canadian psychopath who was formerly partners with Michael. The system is much more than a novelty. Switching between them allows Rockstar to prod us into different parts of the world to explore, without relying on a single character to experience everything. For a map this large, it makes a lot of sense. For clarity, following the release of its single-player expansions The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, GTA IV also ultimately featured three protagonists – and three different lenses through which we could view and interact with Liberty City. Similarly, it was a really smart way of squeezing more value out of the map, and drilling down on parts of it Niko Bellic’s story never really took him to. But while you could certainly regard this as a first draft of a multi-protagonist approach, you can’t switch between them in real time in GTA IV; you have to pause and load into the expansions separately. In GTA V, the transition between characters is far, far more rapid, and occurs after just a brief zoom out and back in again, dropping you into Michael, Franklin, or Trevor’s life in the middle of whatever they happen to be doing at the time – which may well be dropping a man off a bridge. The transitions give the illusion that these guys continue to exist beyond the missions in which they appear. GTA V’s missions are typically far more varied and layered than those in GTA IV. After experimenting with it in The Ballad of Gay Tony, GTA V introduced mission checkpoints and finally shed what had arguably become the most frustrating characteristic of the series – the need to completely start from scratch after failing a mission. This is what allows GTA V’s missions to be longer and regularly more wild than ever. With checkpoints as a safety net, Rockstar could really push the boat out with what it asked us to attempt – free from the sometimes debilitating concern that messing up at the last minute will result in a long drive and a lot of backtracking over things we’ve already done. Of course, the highlight here is the focus on multilayed heists, taking the fan-favourite Three Leaf Clover bank robbery mission from GTA IV and blowing that concept out to make it the central pillar of GTA V’s campaign. There are multiple big scores that can be tackled in overtly different ways, something made easy to experiment with thanks to the ability to easily replay missions from a list of those you’ve previously completed. With the exception of The Ballad of Gay Tony, in past GTA games, the only way to play the missions again was to start over from the beginning. The heists are where the three-character structure becomes most effective. We’re not just passengers on these huge marquee missions; rather, GTA V builds elaborate on ramps to these heists focused on planning and preparation which typically draw on the different skills and traits of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor. It gives the heists, and the campaign as a whole, a sense of scale and variety that would’ve been difficult to achieve through a single character. Beyond the multiple protagonists and the escalation in mission variety, GTA V also made major changes to the car handling and significant refinements to the shooting. Vehicles are certainly more approachable to drive in GTA V than they are in GTA IV; they brake hard and respond sharply to steering input. The result isn’t superficial or overly light, but it does feel very grippy. It’s a handling model that I think is particularly suited to sure-footed sports cars, although I have to concede a part of me prefers the way older vehicles feel with the “slidey cars” cheat on. It’s just more drift-friendly. In terms of vehicle variety, however, GTA V is very much a welcome shift back to the broad spectrum available in GTA: San Andreas after things were scaled back significantly in GTA IV. As a result, one minute you could be fanging an 18-wheeler down the freeway, and the next kicking tyres and lighting fires in a fighter jet. GTA V dialled things up rather than back, so go ahead: land that jumbo on the beach and escape via a jet ski. Why the hell not? Combat was polished too, with more nimble movement and more dependable cover shooting. The highlight for me is the sound of firefights, as guns bark and bullets thunk into car panels. It’s brilliant stuff. The integration of the weapon wheel, which functions similarly to Red Dead Redemption and Max Payne 3, also means you can carry way more hardware – as well as multiple weapons within a single class. The weapon wheel stores all of the weapons you collect and you’ll never lose them, even if they run out of ammo or you get busted. When GTA V launched on Xbox 360 and PS3 in September 2013, both of those consoles were approaching the end of their lifespans. With the Xbox One and PS4 arriving in November that same year, you could probably make a strong case that GTA V felt like the last great statement of that generation. Many people did. However, I think there’s more to it than that. A couple of weeks before its September 17 release, I was fortunate enough to conduct the world’s first hands-on with GTA V for IGN. Revisiting and playing it again so extensively this week has very effectively taken me back to how blown away I was in that moment. I was stunned by what I was playing, and utterly convinced GTA V was outright good enough to upstage both Microsoft and Sony’s new consoles. In fact, I wrote never mind November; the next generation will start when Rockstar says it does. In 2013, that was a comment reflective of just how ahead of its time I believed GTA V was; that it was simply streets ahead of its peers, squeezing next-generation scope and ambition out of a console that first launched in 2005. Simply put, it felt like a new benchmark for an era that hadn’t even officially arrived yet. On September 3, 2013 – two weeks before GTA V came out – maybe that’s a bold claim. But with new and improved versions of GTA V going on to loom large over the generation to follow, and then doing it all over again for the generation after that – all to the tune of 230 million copies – I don’t think it was ever an exaggeration. Grand Theft Auto V was a game so preposterously future-proof upon its 2013 launch on Xbox 360 and PS3 that its subsequent ports to modern machines remain the benchmark for open-world action-driving games. At the conclusion of this GTA Legacy Review project I find myself too emotionally attached to the PS2 pair of Vice City and San Andreas to push past my adoration for the style and soundtracks of those period piece classics and place anything above them but, make no mistake, there are very few games I’ve played more than GTA V. Combining an enormous and extraordinarily detailed world, three compelling protagonists, a thrilling set of varied missions and heists, and the foundation for a world of multiplayer that is simply a whole separate discussion, GTA V is the peak of the series. At least for the next few weeks, that is. title: Cadillac Celebrates 125 Years With A $239,000 Escalade-V - Autoguide.com
content: Cadillac is marking its 125th birthday with an Escalade V-Series. The new special-edition 2027 Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series starts at $239,000, bringing a massive price tag, exclusive styling, and collector-focused details to the brand’s supercharged full-size SUV. Limited to just 252 examples, the special edition is available in two exclusive finishes: Midnight Stone Frost and Vibrant White Tricoat. Each SUV rides on unique 24-inch (!) forged wheels and features carbon-fiber accents around the grille, rear fascia, and mirror caps. Blue brake calipers, dark-finished badges, and illuminated V8 Heritage puddle lamps further distinguish the anniversary model. Cadillac has carried the special treatment into the cabin as well, which is good because the exterior changes frankly aren't much. The interior combines black and gray upholstery with Santorini Blue stitching and seat belts. Exclusive floor mats, anniversary badging, illuminated door-sill plates, and a matching blue key fob round out the upgrades. Buyers can also select their vehicle identification number and collector serial number, adding another layer of exclusivity. Still, not a ton to show for the "special edition," but we appreciate that they're doing it. Sure would be better if it was a CT5-V Blackwing, wouldn't it? Underneath the (pretty minimalistic) cosmetic changes, the Escalade-V remains mechanically unchanged. Its hand-built, supercharged 6.2-liter V8 produces 682 horsepower and 653 lb-ft of torque, delivering the same performance as the standard model. That makes the anniversary edition more about rarity than outright speed. At $239,000, it commands a $66,805 premium over the regular 2027 Escalade-V, which starts at $172,195. Orders are open in the United States and Canada. With production capped at 252 units, Cadillac is betting that its most devoted customers will pay (a whole lot) extra to own a piece of its history. title: Cadillac Turns 125 With a Special Escalade-V That Costs $239,000 and Is Limited to 252 Units - MotorBiscuit
content: Cadillac, founded in 1902, is marking 125 years, and it has attached a year to every car in a very small run of Escalades. The 2027 Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series will be built in just 252 examples, with each of its two exterior colors getting vehicles numbered from 1902 through 2027 to represent the span of the brand’s history. This follows the Mexico-only Escalade-V Checo Pérez Edition, limited to 11 units in honor of Cadillac’s F1 driver. Kristian Aquilina, Vice President, Global Cadillac, put the intent plainly: “The Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series celebrates Cadillac’s heritage and our uncompromising approach to performance luxury,” he said. “From its exclusive design to its highly limited availability, this special edition gives collectors a distinctive way to celebrate Cadillac’s legacy while looking ahead to its future.” The color story starts inside. A two-tone black and gray cabin is lifted by Santorini Blue stitching, and the seatbelts match it. Illuminated sill plates mark the occasion as the doors open, while exclusive interior badging, special floor mats, and a blue key fob carry the theme through the rest of the cabin. Each detail is small, but together they make the interior feel purpose-built rather than a standard Escalade-V with a sticker. Outside, the treatment is more restrained. Carbon fiber covers the grille surround, lower rear fascia, and mirror caps, and the engine bay gets a carbon fiber cover as well. Unique forged 24-inch wheels and blue brake calipers add contrast, and Heritage V8 puddle lamps provide the finishing touch. Blue calipers behind the wheels echo the blue found inside the cabin, tying the two halves of the car together. Paint choices are deliberately limited. Buyers can pick Midnight Stone Frost or Vibrant White Tricoat, so the details above, not the color, are what separate each car from a regular Escalade-V. Cadillac revealed the SUV in Austin, Texas, ahead of the United States Grand Prix. It starts at approximately $239,000, including destination freight but excluding taxes, title, and dealer fees, with final pricing set by dealers. The SUV will be sold in the United States and Canada, and orders are now open. Your email address will not be published. title: Chris Sutton gives Liverpool v Brighton prediction as he backs 6-month sequence to continue - Yahoo Sports
content: Chris Sutton is predicting one unenviable Liverpool sequence to continue when they host Brighton in the Premier League on Sunday. Incredibly, the fixture will mark six months to the day that the Reds last won a top-flight match at Anfield (3-1 v Crystal Palace), with five subsequent league games in L4 ending in either a draw or a loss dating back to the final month of last season. This weekend Andoni Iraola's side come up against a Seagulls outfit who couldn't be in better form, winning their last four Premier League matches by a combined scoreline of 15-0, including a three-goal thrashing of champions Arsenal. Liverpool beat Brighton twice at Anfield last term, but Sutton believes the visitors will extend their winning run in the division and extend the Red's wait for a home win in the league. In his weekly Premier League predictions piece for BBC Sport, the former Chelsea striker wrote: 'Liverpool have an extra 48 hours to prepare for this game – they played Villarreal at home on Tuesday, while Brighton are away in the Czech Republic on Thursday. 'I don't think it will make any difference, though, because the way that the Seagulls play, I am expecting them to go to Anfield and win. 'This has the makings of a great game but, while Liverpool have had a couple of good results, I am still not convinced by them. Andoni Iraola's side are a work in progress with a tendency to empty their midfield and that means Brighton can hurt them.' Sutton has gone for the Seagulls to come away with a 3-1 victory. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Away wins have been very rare in recent meeting between these two teams – in 11 league and cup clashes since the start of 2022/23, only once has the visiting side emerged triumphant, so at least that's one good omen for Liverpool. The Reds have quietly been building momentum under Iraola, winning seven of their last nine games in all competitions, but victory over a red-hot Brighton would probably be their best result of the season so far. The hosts would have to achieve it without several first-team regulars including Dominik Szoboszlai and Hugo Ekitike. Also, it remains to be seen whether Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola will be fit to feature, although the latter underwent an individual recovery session on Thursday. Liverpool's defence has looked brittle of late, with 10 goals conceded in their last four matches, and the Seagulls are the highest scorers in the Premier League at present with 23 already in this campaign (the Reds have only nine). Sutton is right about Brighton's capacity to do damage if the home side aren't on it from the start, but Iraola's side have plenty of quality in their own ranks and are good enough to take down any opposition when at their best and end their six-month wait for a top-flight win at Anfield.

title: Bears v Patriots - Bears prevail with a statement win - Windy City Gridiron
content: The Chicago Bears move to 5-2 after a statement win over the defending AFC champion New England Patriots. Forty years after Super Bowl XX, the Bears and Patriots meet again under the lights at Soldier Field—this time on Thursday Night Football, with both clubs sitting at 4-2 and fighting for early-season positioning in their divisions. The night carries extra weight for Chicago: the franchise is honoring Mike Ditka, the iconic coach of that 1985 championship team, who passed away less than two weeks ago, with handout mustaches to attending fans. On the field, it’s a high-profile collision of the top two quarterbacks from the 2024 draft—Caleb Williams, the No. 1 overall pick now operating in Ben Johnson’s system after a recent return from injury, and Drake Maye, the No. 3 pick who has helped New England string together three straight wins after a shaky start. Both defenses entered the night ranked among the league’s best in scoring and against the run, setting up a physical, low-margin matchup. Instead, the first half delivered explosive plays, a critical end-zone interception, and a last-second touchdown that kept the Patriots within striking distance heading into the locker room. Add Windy City Gridiron as a preferred source to see more of our reporting on Google. New England’s opening drive stalled when Kyler Gordon sacked Drake Maye on fourth down, giving Chicago good field position. Cairo Santos cashed in with a 43-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. The Bears’ offense then hit a coverage breakdown. Luther Burden III took a short throw and raced 58 yards into the red zone. One play later, D’Andre Swift finished it with a 4-yard touchdown run. Santos’ extra point made it 10-0 with under two minutes left in the quarter. Gooch Observation: Chicago’s early efficiency and Burden’s explosiveness set the tone. The Patriots’ offense looked stuck, and the Bears’ run defense (and Gordon’s pressure) limited New England early. Gooch Hot take: Burden looked like the best player on the field in the opening 15 minutes. The 58-yarder wasn’t just a big play—it exposed a Patriots secondary that got caught flat-footed. Also, I hate to say it, but this defense just looks faster with TJ Edwards and some of the older defensive players on the sidelines. New England finally found rhythm. A 9-play, 74-yard drive ended with Drake Maye stretching across the goal line on a 7-yard scramble. The officials initially ruled it short, but Mike Vrabel challenged and won. The score cut the lead to 10-7. Gooch Hot Take: Had it been called a TD initially, I wouldn’t really have a problem. But if the ankle is down or the ball hits bf the ball crosses - its down. You’re going to tell me that was clear and obvious? It’s just clear the NFL has utterly abandoned its preference for the call on the field. Chicago answered after a big Zavion Thomas kickoff return. The drive stalled in the red zone (penalties and an incomplete to Rome Odunze), but Santos added a field goal for 13-7. The momentum swung hard on the next possession. Maye lofted a pass into the end zone that D’Marco Jackson read perfectly and intercepted (Jackson >>>> TJ). Chicago took over and immediately scored: Williams hit Burden on a short pass, and Burden took it the rest of the way (helped by downfield blocking from Colston Loveland) for a touchdown. 20-7. It was looking like it was all coming up Bears. I had mentally already headed into halftime. Perhaps that’s what the Bears defense did - because, in an utterly inexplicable, inexcusable series of plays, the Bears allowed the Patriots to score a TD. On the final play of the half, Rhamondre Stevenson zig-zagged through the Bears’ defense for a 48-yard touchdown. The score made it 20-14 at intermission. Chicago will get the ball to start the second half. It frankly reminded me of the dark days under Eberflus when we allowed an inexplicable TD by the Arizona Cardinals at the end of a half in a game we should have won. Gooch Quip: The first half felt like two different games—Burden and the Bears building a comfortable lead, then Stevenson reminding everyone that Thursday Night Football doesn’t do quiet endings. Chicago has the lead, but the Patriots just made sure the second half won’t be a formality. A missed opportunity to be sure. Chicago wasted no time putting the Stevenson buzzer-beater behind them. Taking the second-half kickoff, the Bears marched 72 yards in nine plays and finished with Caleb Williams’ 12-yard touchdown pass to Colston Loveland. The score pushed the lead to 27-14 and gave the home crowd early breathing room. New England responded in kind. Drake Maye found rookie tight end Eli Raridon for a 30-yard touchdown, cutting the deficit back to one score at 27-21. The Patriots overcame penalties on the drive and showed they could still move the ball through the air. Gooch Observation: Both offenses looked sharper out of the break than they had at times in the first half. Loveland’s red-zone connection gave Williams his second touchdown pass of the night, while Raridon provided Maye another reliable target. I have some questions about our defense. Gooch Hot take: The third quarter was essentially a wash—each team scored once—but Chicago’s ability to score first after receiving the kickoff kept the Patriots chasing all night. The final period featured field-goal drama and a late scramble. Cairo Santos’ 53-yard attempt doinked off the upright, briefly giving New England life and field position. Later, with the game still in the balance, the Bears drove into range, but Christian Barmore sacked Williams and appeared to push them out of field-goal range. Santos answered anyway, drilling a career-long 58-yarder to make it 30-21 with just over a minute left. The Patriots managed a quick field goal to pull within 30-24, then attempted an onside kick. Rome Odunze recovered it, and Chicago ran out the clock. GOOCH Quip: The second half wasn’t as chaotic as the first, but Santos’ long kick and Odunze’s recovery made sure the Bears left Soldier Field with the win they had been protecting since early in the third quarter. In a game that opened with nods to Super Bowl XX and Mike Ditka, the Bears did just enough to protect an early lead and close out a 30-24 Thursday Night Football win that moves them to 5-2. Caleb Williams was efficient and mistake-free (22-of-33, 308 yards, two touchdowns), Luther Burden provided the explosive plays that set the tone, and Cairo Santos delivered the dagger with a career-long 58-yard field goal after a sack nearly took the points off the board. Drake Maye kept the Patriots in it with 321 yards and two scores of his own, and Rhamondre Stevenson’s half-ending 48-yard catch-and-run made sure the night stayed tense, but New England’s first-half end-zone interception and inability to force a late stop left them short. Chicago recovered the onside kick to seal it, outdueling the No. 3 pick from their draft class on a night when both offenses produced but only one team consistently answered. GOOCH FINAL THOUGHT: The Bears dominated this game in all phases. Only a few mistakes allowed the Patriots to stay in the game. What amazed me is that Caleb and this team, on both sides, refuses to allow game breaking plays to defeat them. The Bears take your shot and keep on going. And this team has made a statement in going to 5-2 against last year’s Super Bowl participant. BEAR DOWN! title: NetChoice v. Bonta (California Censorship Labels) - NetChoice
content:
Case Status: Complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California
Latest Update: October 22, 2026 
Attorneys: Websites cannot be forced to act as mouthpieces for California’s views about social media. NetChoice’s newest lawsuit challenges California’s latest attempt to control and compel online speech. AB 56 forces websites to display California’s preferred message about social media use-–messages that cannot be skipped by users and get larger and more frequent over time. And just like laws in Colorado and Minnesota that NetChoice is already challenging, AB 56 is flatly unconstitutional. The goal is to deter users from online services and push the government’s controversial views on social media. This is compelled speech, a direct violation of the First Amendment. California’s AB 56 singles out the websites where free speech thrives today, especially on political and cultural issues. The First Amendment bars the government from making private actors speak for it, whether the medium be a billboard, a newspaper, or a website. States cannot do by “warning label” what they’re forbidden from doing by outright ban, and trying to chill speech through stigma is still censorship. A federal court already blocked Colorado’s nearly identical law in NetChoice v. Weiser, and California’s is even more extreme. California is using legitimate concerns about mental health as cover for a law that’s really about power. The science on how online services affect mental health and well-being is still emerging and contradictory, and it’s even thinner for adults. There’s no credible evidence that a government warning label improves youth well-being. Users will ultimately pay the price. The state’s goal is to annoy people away from websites whose content it dislikes, cluttering their screens with government messages they must sit through no matter how many times they’ve seen them. Lawmakers who want a better online environment for kids should pursue constitutional measures like those in NetChoice’s Digital Safety Shield for America. California is free to share its own views through public campaigns and resources, but it can’t force private websites to speak for it. NetChoice’s complaint filed on October 22, 2026, in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.

title: V. Fern Young-Ewell - bendbulletin.com
content: V. Fern Young-Ewell passed away on September 28, 2026, at the age of 94. Fern was born to William and Sadie Scott Smalley November 7, 1931, in Nowata, Oklahoma. The family relocated to Oregon in August 1937, when she was 5 years old. She attended Lone Pine School, Terrebonne Grade School and graduated from Redmond Union High School in 1949. She participated in many sports and was a majorette representing the Redmond Panthers. After graduation, she attended Central Oregon Community College, focusing on business. In 1949, she married Donald Young, her high school sweetheart. They had three children, David, Rita and Carla. Fern worked as a secretary for the Deschutes County 4-H Club Agent, Lincoln-Mercury and a local attorney. She worked several years at the Deschutes Farmers Coop, ending as the assistant manager. The family lived on the dairy farm until 1967. During this time, Fern milked cows, drove hay and potato trucks and picked clods from a potato combine with Don. Don and Fern purchased the Golden Age Guest Ranch in Terrebonne and operated it for 13 years. They also owned Premier Bowl, Young’s Hobby Shop, Young’s Physical Fitness Center and several rental properties. Fern was past-President of the Redmond Lady Elks and a notary for many years. She worked on the election board and volunteered for the Deschutes County Hotline for troubled teenagers. Fern was elected president of the Redmond Senior Center in 2011 and 2014 (six years) and as the Deschutes County Pioneer Queen in 2015. While raising her children, Fern always made time to attend their many activities: track meets and motorcycle races with David and 4-H and rodeos with Rita and Carla. She was always there for her children and grandchildren. Don, Fern’s husband of 50 years, passed away in April 1999. She married Bill Ewell of Kennewick, Washington, in September 2000. He passed away in 2019. Fern enjoyed traveling in her motorhome, fishing, playing cards, dancing and meeting new people. Above all, she loved her family and friends. She is survived by David (LuAnn) Young of Spokane, Washington, Rita (Jim) Smith of Portland, Oregon, and Carla (Dan) McGinley of Prineville, Oregon; seven grandchildren; 21 great-grandchildren; nine great-great-grandchildren; and numerous others who called her Mom and Grandma. Fern was a very generous, kind, giving and loving person. In her spirit of giving, we suggest donating blood to the Red Cross or monetary donations to Hospice or a charity of your choice in her honor. title: Is This Special Edition 2027 Cadillac Escalade-V Really Worth $239K? - MotorTrend
content:
The 2027 Cadillac Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series marks how far the American luxury automaker has come. Cadillac was founded in August 1902 and rolled out its first cars, a pair of horseless carriages powered by 10-hp single-cylinder engines, just three months later. For 2027, the American luxury brand will celebrate its founding with the Cadillac Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series, a limited-edition model with a 682-hp supercharged V-8. Anniversary models will come painted in Vibrant White Tricoat or Midnight Stone Frost, the latter of which is exclusive to this special edition. Cadillac will build 126 examples in each color with every car getting a placard dedicating it to a single year from 1902 through 2027. That means the total production run amounts to just 252 examples. You can identify these limited-edition V’s by their unique forged 24-inch wheels over blue brake calipers and the carbon-fiber grille surround, lower rear fascia, mirror caps, and engine cover. Special puddle lamps project a heritage V-8 logo onto the ground at night while the exterior badging features a dark finish. The interior is covered in black and Sheer Gray upholstery accented with Santorini Blue stitching and seat belts in a nod to the V-Series Mondrian logo. Special illuminated sill plates pay homage to Cadillac’s long and rich history of building V-8 engines. There are also premium floor mats, a blue key fob, and the requisite interior badging. To sweeten the deal, buyers have the option of choosing their own VIN. Mechanically, the 125th Anniversary Collector Series is identical to any other Escalade-V with a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8, MagneRide dampers, and all-wheel-drive. We tested an Escalade-V back in 2023 and clocked a 4.7-second run from 0–60 mph. That might not sound all that quick by today’s standards, but don’t get hung up on one number. The engine sound alone might be reason enough to own an Escalade-V. At a price of approximately $239,000, the 125th Anniversary Collector Series costs almost $69,000 more than the run-of-the-mill Escalade-V. It will be sold in both the U.S. and Canada and can be ordered through dealers now. Cadillac launched the Collector Series in 2022 with the first 250 units of the CT4-V Blackwing and the CT5-V Blackwing. Last year the automaker celebrated its entry into Formula 1 racing with a 26-car run of the CT5-V Blackwing F1 Collector Series that featured a power increase from 668 to 685 hp and an F1 logo stamped into the front doors. I fell in love with car magazines during sixth-grade silent reading time and soon realized that the editors were being paid to drive a never-ending parade of new cars and write stories about their experiences. Could any job be better? The answer was obvious to 11-year-old me.
By the time I reached high school, becoming an automotive journalist wasn’t just a distant dream, it was a goal. I joined the school newspaper and weaseled my way into media days at the Detroit auto show. With a new driver’s license in my wallet, I cold-called MotorTrend’s Detroit editor, who graciously agreed to an informational interview and then gave me the advice that set me on the path to where I am today. Get an engineering degree and learn to write, he said, and everything else would fall into place.
I left nothing to chance and majored in both mechanical engineering and journalism at Michigan State, where a J-school prof warned I’d become a “one-note writer” if I kept turning in stories about cars for every assignment. That sounded just fine by me, so I talked my way into GM’s Lansing Grand River Assembly plant for my next story.
My child-like obsession with cars started to pay off soon after. In 2007, I won an essay contest to fly to the Frankfurt auto show and drive the Saturn Astra with some of the same writers I had been reading since sixth grade. Winning that contest launched my career. I wrote for Jalopnik and Edmunds, interned at Automobile, finished school, and turned down an engineering job with Honda for full-time employment with Automobile. In the years since, I’ve written for Car and Driver, The New York Times, and now, coming full circle, MotorTrend.
It has been a dream. A big chunk of this job is exactly what it looks like: playing with cars. I’m happiest when the work involves affordable sporty hatchbacks, expensive sports cars, manual transmissions, or any technology that requires I learn something to understand how it works, but I’m not picky. title: YouTuber arrested after popular Indian finance influencer's suicide - BBC
content: A 27-year-old finance influencer's suicide in India has been mired in allegations of cyberbullying and started a conversation around who should give financial advice to investors. V Harish - who ran a hugely popular Instagram account called "Finance with Harish" - was found dead on Tuesday morning at his home near Chennai, capital of the southern state of Tamil Nadu. His suicide came just weeks after his account was disabled by Meta after complaints of irregularities. In a complaint lodged with the police, his father J Vinayagam has alleged that his son took his life because of online harassment by Jason Samuel, a YouTuber and CEO of tech-centric venture studio Zemuria. Police arrested Samuel on Thursday under suspicion of trying to "extort money from Harish" and posting "defamatory videos against him on social media". BBC Tamil has not been able to reach him for comment. Earlier, he denied wrongdoing in a post on X. The case has brought into focus the growing influence of financial content creators in India, where millions of first-time investors increasingly turn to social media for market advice. Harish began posting videos about finance and investing around five years ago, building a substantial online following. Over the years, he published more than 1,500 videos and amassed more than 1.3 million Instagram followers. He described himself as a financial adviser to "millionaires" and "high-net-worth individuals". He often used music, film clips and photos of global political leaders to make dramatic videos while talking about the rise and fall of the share market and prices of gold and silver. The videos, which broke down financial issues in simple terms, became hugely popular as they coincided with a rapid expansion in India's retail investor base, especially since the 2020 Covid-19 pandemic. The country's largest stock exchange, the National Stock Exchange, said earlier this year it now had more than 130 million unique investors registered with it as opposed to under 30 million in 2019. But in September, Meta took down Harish's Instagram page after receiving complaints he was not registered with Indian market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) - which is required under law to be able to offer investment advice or manage client portfolios. A back-up account, which gained over 60,000 followers in a short time, was also subsequently taken down following complaints from social media users and others. A few other accounts in his name remain on Instagram, though with much smaller followings - and it's not clear who runs them. According to Harish's friends and family, he recorded a video message before his death in which he said that "five years of hard work has been stolen" from him, news channel NDTV reported. The video, which has also been shared widely on social media, shows him speaking in Tamil and then switching to English to say "I'm very sorry" to his parents, sister, friends and followers. Police say Harish's father J Vinayagam has blamed "cyberbullying, defamatory social media posts and repeated blocking of his channels" for his son's suicide and named Jason Samuel in his complaint registered at Kanathur police station near Chennai. Samuel had posted a video on his YouTube channel on 18 October questioning Harish's credentials since he did not have Sebi or Amfi (Association of Mutual Funds in India) registrations. In it, he mentioned that Harish's Instagram account had been disabled following complaints. This, Vinayagam says, triggered severe online harassment and led to pressures that drove his son to take his own life. "We demand that a proper investigation be conducted and legal action be taken against Jason Samuel and his accomplices, who spread defamation on social media and caused mental distress through cyberbullying," his complaint states. A police statement says Vinayagam's complaint was registered under "abetment to suicide" and preliminary investigations found Samuel had a "role in this case". "[Samuel] will be produced before court and sent to judicial custody," it says. Samuel has defended the video in which he flagged Harish's lack of credentials saying he was acting in the consumer interest. In a statement on X, Samuel said he was "deeply saddened, heavily grieving, shocked and frozen at what has happened and I mourn the loss of life". He however, rejected allegations of "cyber-bullying" Harish. "I have not cyber-bullied him. I pointed out his lack of licence and authority, misrepresentation of licence and fraud... his illegal activity. "I literally asked him in the video to come back and do this with a proper Sebi licence. I never intended or expected this drastic measure to happen and I mourn the loss," he wrote. If you're having thoughts of suicide, or know someone that might be, you can find support lines in India via the AASRA website or globally via Befrienders Worldwide. In the UK you can call the Samaritans Helpline on 116 123 or visit samaritans.org. Half a dozen elite British schools are chasing growth in India amid a boom in its  wealthy population. One person has died after being swept away by waves in Taiwan's Liuqiu island, authorities say. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed a business and energy agenda over diplomacy on his second trip to India this year. Indian workers are being paid to film themselves at work and the footage is used to train AI. The attack on Shroff has revived memories of the 1990s, when gangsters wielded influence over the industry. Copyright 2026 BBC. All rights reserved. title: How to watch Bournemouth v AC Milan, team news, predicted line-ups and more - Yahoo Sports
content: Bournemouth welcome Italian giants AC Milan in the Europa League, looking for a memorable win. The Cherries have won their first two games in their maiden European campaign, with victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz. Milan boss Ruben Amorim returns to England for the first time since leaving Manchester United in January. His side will be looking for a third consecutive victory after wins against Salzburg and Atalanta. Here's everything you need to know ahead of the game… Bournemouth v AC Milan kicks off at 8pm UK time at the Vitality Stadium. The game will be aired on TNT Sports 1, HBO Max (UK) and TNT Sports Ultimate. Bournemouth will continue to be without star player Eli Junior Kroupi who was back in training this week after injuring his foot in pre-season. However, this fixture comes too early for the Frenchman. Alex Scott will also be unavailable after picking up an injury during the international break. Julián Araujo is also injured. Defender Veljko Milosavljevíc has been in action for the under-21 team as he steps up his recovery from an injury sustained in May. Milan will be without defender Matteo Gabbia and winger Alexis Saelemaekers, who remain sidelined. Filippo Terracciano is also unavailable after being sent off against Salzburg. Amorim confirmed that striker Gonçalo Romes has a fitness issue, although it is "nothing serious." The manager also said that Alphadjo Cissè will play after scoring a hat-trick against Salzburg. Marco Rose has played down talk of this being the biggest game in Bournemouth's history. He said: "It is a huge game and we are looking forward to it, but the club has played a much bigger game before. "Many years ago, after the points deduction, they needed to win their last game at home [against Grimsby] and Steve Fletcher scored the winning goal. That's the foundation of why we are here now, playing these kinds of games. "We feel we're in a good spot. We have created a good momentum for ourselves now and we should use that to our advantage." Amorim has praised his opponents and looked back on his time as Manchester United manager. "Every match is important. This will be our third group-stage game and another test of where we stand. We're going there to win. "There are always technical and tactical aspects we need to improve, and we still have a long way to go. Bournemouth has quality and plays at a high tempo. They have some excellent players who are strong in one-on-one situations. "They've made a few changes since I faced them as Manchester United manager, but they haven't lost their identity. I'm returning to England as AC Milan manager. I loved Manchester United, but I'm not thinking about the past. I feel I'm a better coach now, but I believe I'm still the same person I was before." Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Christie; Tavenier, Kluivert, Gannon-Doak; Evanilson. Milan (3-4-2-1): Maignan; Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic; Chukwueze, Musah, Rabiot, Bartesaghi; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Camarda.

title: The Supreme Court Upholds Preliminary Injunction in Kingdom v. Trump,… - Human Rights Campaign
content:
by

                Aneesha Pappy
              
•
                October 21, 2026 HRC President Kelley Robinson: “This decision protects trans inmates from the administration’s attempt to steamroll constitutional rights for now, but the fight to uphold the dignity and respect our community deserves is far from over.” WASHINGTON, DC— Today, the Supreme Court upheld the lower court’s preliminary injunction in Kingdom v. Trump, blocking Trump’s executive order that prohibits the federal Bureau of Prisons from providing transition-related medical care to transgender incarcerated people in federal facilities while the case moves through the courts. Human Rights Campaign President Kelley Robinson released the following statement: “Today, trans people in federal prisons can keep getting the care they need. Denying access to critical medical care for incarcerated people simply because they are trans is discriminatory, cruel and flies in the face of our Eighth Amendment protections. Trump and MAGA extremists are obsessed with targeting our community and undermining access to essential healthcare, defying the recommendations of every major medical association in the country. This decision protects incarcerated trans people from the administration’s attempt to steamroll over constitutional rights for now, but the fight to uphold the dignity and respect our community deserves is far from over.” Kingdom v. Trump challenges an executive order issued earlier this year by Trump prohibiting the federal Bureau of Prisons from providing transition-related medical care for incarcerated transgender people in federal prisons and detention centers. The executive order also mandated the transfer of transgender women held in federal facilities to men’s facilities. With support by the ACLU, the ACLU of DC and the Transgender Law Center, the class action lawsuit was filed on behalf of three transgender inmates, arguing that the executive order violates the U.S. Constitution’s Eighth Amendment protections against “cruel and unusual punishments” by denying access to medically-necessary healthcare. In June of this year, the plaintiffs were granted a preliminary injunction blocking the enforcement of the executive order by a federal district court judge — which has now been upheld. The case will continue to be adjudicated in the District Court for the District of Columbia. The Human Rights Campaign (HRC) is the nation’s largest LGBTQ+ civil rights organization working to achieve equality for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ+) people, with 4 million members and supporters. The HRC Foundation (a 501(c)(3)) works to ensure LGBTQ+ people are safe, seen and supported where it matters most: at school, at work and in every community across the country. From the courtroom to the classroom, from Congress to corporate America, HRC and the HRC Foundation build power through partnerships, storytelling, and action—working to create a future rooted in equity, freedom and belonging for all LGBTQ+ people.
